Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Inc. Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a telephone, or click the Q&A button in the webcast platform if joining online. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables Inc.'s results for the Q3 FY2024. Joining me on today's call are Sarah Kline, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Torres, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer; Nina Gupta, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Kim, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Kline.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Solara Renewables continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in Q3 FY2024. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance, starting with one of our highest-growth areas: storage deployment and hybrid project updates. As you know, we're at the forefront of transforming intermittent renewables into dispatchable, firm power through our integrated storage solutions and hybrid co-location strategies. This segment represented 28% of our overall revenue in Q3, up from 19% year-over-year, driven by surging demand for grid stability amid rising renewable penetration and extreme weather events.

In Q3, we achieved first energy from an additional 650 MW / 1,300 MWh of battery energy storage systems, bringing our global operational portfolio to 3.2 GW / 6.4 GWh—more than double what we had at this time last year. This includes the full commercialization of our flagship 300 MW / 600 MWh Gateway project in ERCOT, Texas, which is now delivering ancillary services at a blended revenue stack exceeding $65/kW-year. Utilization hit 72% in Q3, with frequency regulation capturing 45% of dispatch hours, arbitrage 30%, and the balance from capacity payments under ERCOT's ORDC auctions.

Technically, we're leveraging next-gen lithium iron phosphate cells from our strategic partner CATL, achieving round-trip efficiencies of 92.5% at the pack level—up 2 points from our prior NMC deployments—thanks to our proprietary four-quadrant power conversion systems with 99% inverter efficiency. We've also integrated advanced energy management systems with our AI-driven optimization platform, which uses machine learning to forecast duck curve dynamics and maximize value stacking. In California, under CAISO's Resource Adequacy framework, our 200 MW / 400 MWh Diablo Canyon BESS is outperforming peers, with a 15% uplift in net revenue from non-energy markets due to real-time bidding via our automated market participation tools.

Regionally, Texas remains our powerhouse, accounting for 55% of new deployments, fueled by ERCOT's record curtailments—over 2.5 TWh in recent years—and the push for black-start capabilities. We're seeing capex costs for standalone BESS drop 22% year-over-year to $145/kWh DC, inclusive of EPC and balance-of-system, positioning us ahead of industry benchmarks. In Australia, our 150 MW / 300 MWh Torrens project in AEMO's South Australia zone went live ahead of schedule, capturing $85/MWh from FCAS markets amid frequency control challenges. Europe is ramping up too: our 100 MW / 200 MWh pilot in the UK's National Grid ESO is testing 4-hour duration with hybrid vanadium flow battery augmentation, de-risking our entry into TSO auctions under reforms.

Looking ahead, our near-term storage backlog stands at 2.1 GW / 4.2 GWh, with 1.2 GW expected to reach COD by year-end 2025. Margins here are robust at 28% EBITDA, bolstered by the IRA's 48C tax credits—we've qualified $450 million to date—and PTC eligibility for storage-only assets.

Shifting to hybrid project updates, where we're truly differentiating. Hybrids—co-locating solar PV or wind with BESS—are achieving 60-70% capacity factors versus 25-35% for standalone renewables, unlocking premium PPA pricing of $45-55/MWh all-in. In Q3, we energized 450 MW of hybrid capacity, including the 250 MWdc / 100 MWac / 200 MWh Lone Star Solar+Storage hybrid in West Texas, our first to stack solar ITC with storage PTC under the IRA's hybrid adder. This project's 4-hour storage ratio is optimizing for evening peak shave, with modeled IRR north of 12% at a $35/MWh PPA escalation.

Our hybrid pipeline is explosive: 4.8 GWdc under construction or late-stage development, valued at $6.2 billion in enterprise value. Key milestones include the 600 MWdc / 240 MWac / 480 MWh Alamo hybrid in Texas, COD Q4 2024, with a 15-year PPA from a major hyperscaler at $52/MWh; the 400 MWdc / 100 MW / 400 MWh Mojave hybrid in California; the 350 MWdc / 140 MWac / 280 MWh Riverina hybrid in Australia; and a 200 MWdc / 80 MW / 160 MWh pilot in PJM. Hybrids mitigate curtailment risks—down 15% in ERCOT hybrids vs. solar-only—and enable virtual power plants. We're piloting a 500 MW VPP in CAISO with PG&E, projecting $10 million in annual credits. On the tech front, we're advancing long-duration energy storage pilots: a 10 MW / 100-hour iron-air system co-located with 50 MW wind, targeting DOE grants. Bifacial PV modules at 24% efficiency paired with advanced turbines are standardizing our configs.

Market tailwinds are aligned: global BESS deployments hit 70 GW last year, with hybrids comprising 40% of additions. U.S. queue reforms are fast-tracking our 10 GW late-stage pipeline, while EU's REPowerEU mandates 100 GW storage by 2030. Supply chain for LFP cells remains tight, but our offtake agreements through 2026 de-risk this. In summary, storage and hybrids drove 35% core adjusted EBITDA growth in Q3, with FY24 guidance now at $1.2-1.4 billion for this segment.

The other aspects—our CAPEX and OPEX details, revenue and earnings growth, operating capacity and generation output, gross and operating margin trends, PPA pricing trends and extensions, capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets, and tax equity plus project-level financing—demonstrate similar strength, as Michael will detail next.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Michael Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Our financial performance in Q3 FY2024 was exceptional. Revenue reached $1.28 billion, representing a 45% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 30.1%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $287 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $210 million, or $1.45 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Let me dive deeper into these results, starting with revenue and earnings growth analysis. Solara Renewables delivered another blockbuster quarter as a leader in integrated solar PV, onshore and offshore wind, utility-scale BESS, and emerging green hydrogen. Q3 revenue of $1.28 billion was up 45% year-over-year from Q3 2023 and 12% sequentially from Q2. This marks our 10th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, underscoring tailwinds like plummeting hardware costs, hyperscale data center demand, the IRA, and REPowerEU.

Growth was fueled by a 28% increase in contracted backlog to $18.5 billion, 65% tied to investment-grade off-takers via PPAs. Average PPA pricing held at $42/MWh amid LCOE declines—solar down 15% to $28/MWh with TOPCon efficiencies at 23.5%.

By segment: Solar PV, 52% of revenue at $665 million, +52% YoY, with 2.8 GWdc commissioned including the 1.2 GW Desert Sun in California using domestic modules from our Arizona gigafactory and Vertex N-series at 22.8% efficiency. Data center partnerships drove 40% of bookings. Wind, 28% at $358 million, +38% YoY, added 1.1 GW onshore like the 650 MW Midwest Plains and offshore from our Empire Wind stake, with recyclable blades reducing LCOE to $45/MWh. BESS and grid services, 15% at $192 million, +65% YoY, deployed 1.2 GWh with LFP systems and flow battery pilots yielding $250/kW from ancillaries. EPC, O&M, and hydrogen, 5% at $64 million, +30% YoY, with our first 20 MW electrolyzer targeting $2/kg H2.

Regionally: U.S. 68%, +55% YoY via IRA tax equity; Europe 22%, +25% YoY; APAC/Emerging 10%, +20% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA hit $385 million at 30.1% margin, +58% YoY, with gross margins up 420 bps to 28.5% from module deflation, OpEx at 12% of revenue, and positive free cash flow funding repurchases. ROIC improved to 14.2%. We raise FY2024 revenue to $5.3-5.5 billion and EBITDA to $1.45-1.50 billion.

Next, our operating capacity and generation output. We ended Q3 at a record 6.8 GW AC, up 22% YoY from 5.6 GW, including COD of 500 MW like the 250 MW Gemini Solar-plus-Storage with 200 MWh Tesla Megapack and 150 MW wind repower. By tech: solar 4.2 GW (62%), wind 1.9 GW (28%), BESS 700 MW/1.8 GWh (10%). U.S. 5.1 GW (75%), Europe 1.2 GW, APAC 0.5 GW.

Generation output was 4.75 TWh, up 18% YoY, at 25.8% capacity factor. Solar 2.95 TWh (24.2% CF), wind 1.42 TWh (35.1% CF), BESS 380 GWh. Performance ratio improved to 87.5% via O&M tech, despite curtailments. Q4 guidance: 4.9-5.1 TWh at 6.9 GW.

On gross margin and operating margin trends: GAAP gross margin 29.2%, up 210 bps YoY to adjusted 30.1%. Driven by 42% YoY revenue growth, IRA domestic content bonuses lifting pricing to $0.32/W, and shift to N-type PERC/HJT at 23.1% efficiency lowering LCOE 8%. U.S. 32.5%, Europe 27.8%, APAC 25.4%. Operating margin 16.8%, up 180 bps, with SG&A down to 7.2%, R&D at 3.8% on perovskites and solid-state batteries. Q3 guidance 30-31% gross, FY24 29.5-30.5%.

CAPEX and OPEX details further underscore discipline. Q3 CAPEX $482 million, +18% YoY, YTD $1.32 billion toward $1.9-2.1 billion FY24 guidance and 2.8 GW construction. OPEX $287 million, +4% YoY but -12% per MW. EBITDA margins 42% on LCOE under $25/MWh.

CAPEX by tech: solar $265 million (55%, $0.82M/MWdc on TOPCon at 23.5% efficiency); wind $121 million (25%, $1.35M/MW on Vestas V150); BESS $72 million (15%, $285/kWh LFP); clean tech $24 million (5%, 50 MW PEM electrolyzer). Regional: U.S. $337 million (70%), Europe $96 million (20%), APAC/LatAm $49 million (10%). Blended cost down 14% YoY to $0.95M/MW.

OPEX breakdown: O&M $129 million ($12/kW-yr solar, $28/kW-yr wind); SG&A $86 million (6% revenue); R&D $43 million (perovskites, floating wind); other $29 million. Cumulative 22% deflation since 2022 via localization, digital APM at 98.5% availability, remote O&M. FY24 OPEX $1.15-1.20B; FY25 CAPEX $2.4-2.6B.

PPA pricing trends and contract extensions: PPAs are 85% of backlog. New solar averages $32/MWh, +8% YoY; wind $34/MWh. Hybrids $42/MWh premium. U.S. Southwest $35-38/MWh, ERCOT $28-32/MWh. Extensions on 720 MW at $38/MWh, +28% uplift, like Mojave to 2040 at $41/MWh with BESS retrofit monetizing $45 million ITC. PPA 2.0 with dynamic clauses adds yield. Guidance $34/MWh average new pricing.

Capacity addition guidance and pipeline targets: FY24 raised to 2.3-2.5 GW (solar 1.5-1.7 GW, wind 500-600 MW, BESS 300-400 MWh); FY25 3.2-3.7 GW. Pipeline 52 GW gross: advanced 18 GW (85-95% conversion), mid 22 GW, early 12 GW. Net 38 GW at $32/MWh. U.S. 28 GW, Europe 13 GW, APAC/LatAm 11 GW. Hybrids 40% of FY25, supply chain locked, $2B M&A powder.

Tax equity financing and project-level financing: Q3 $1.8 billion closed. Tax equity $1.2 billion for 850 MW at 7.1% yield, leveraging IRA adders to 55-65% ITC. Pipeline $4.5 billion FY25. Project debt $650 million at SOFR+190 bps, green bonds, SSLs. WACC 5.8%, LCOE $25-35/MWh solar.

I'll now turn the call over to Lisa Torres to discuss our project development activities.

Lisa Torres:
Thank you, Michael. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with 52 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring a substantial number of new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

Dr. Raj Patel, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing groundbreaking technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies, including perovskite tandems targeting 30% efficiency and long-duration storage. We believe that these technologies will revolutionize the energy landscape.

Next, Elena Vasquez will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability, achieving high ESG scores through biodiversity net-gain and TCFD-aligned modeling.

Now, Tom Reilly will provide operational highlights.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Elena. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best-in-class practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management, with fleet availability at 98.5% via AI and robotics. We are also investing heavily in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to excel.

Nina Gupta, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Nina Gupta:
Thank you, Tom. We are focused on executing our long-term strategic plan, which includes expanding our presence in key markets, diversifying our product offerings, and strengthening our partnerships. We are also actively exploring new opportunities in emerging areas such as green hydrogen and carbon capture, with pilots aligned to DOE Hubs and EU IPCEI.

And finally, David Kim, can you address our risk management strategies?

David Kim:
Thank you, Nina. We have implemented robust risk management strategies to mitigate potential risks associated with our operations, including market risks, regulatory risks, and environmental risks. We are continuously monitoring and evaluating our risk profile—such as interconnection delays and supply chain issues—and taking proactive steps like hedging 80% of debt and climate scenario analysis to manage these risks effectively.

I'll turn it back to Sarah for closing remarks.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you all. In conclusion, Solara Renewables had a truly exceptional Q3 FY2024. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our unwavering focus on sustainability will continue to drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Doe:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you for the question, John. Green hydrogen is a key pillar of our clean tech R&D, with $24 million in Q3 CAPEX toward our 50 MW PEM electrolyzer pilot partnered with Plug Power, targeting under $2/kg by 2026. This leverages DOE Hydrogen Hubs and EU IPCEI funding. We're also blending H2 offtake in PPAs from curtailed renewables, with a 20 MW project at Texas Blue Horizon using PEM tech. Our pipeline includes 5 GW MoUs with partners like TotalEnergies, expecting H2 to scale to 10% of revenue by 2027 amid $7B DOE support. We've locked supply chains and hedged risks, positioning us for 15% IRRs as LCOE falls.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Sarah Kline:
Great question, Jane. Competition is intensifying, but our edge lies in vertical integration—40% insourced supply chain, 52 GW pipeline with 85% conversion velocity, and hybrids driving 60-70% capacity factors. Unlike peers, we stack revenues via VPPs, ancillaries, and IRA adders, with EBITDA margins at 30% and ROIC 14%. Strategic M&A like our 800 MW bolt-on and partnerships de-risk queues, while tech like TOPCon at 23.5% efficiency and LFP BESS keeps LCOE under $25/MWh. We're selective on 15%+ IRR projects, outpacing NextEra and Orsted through execution.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

David Kim:
Thanks, Mike. Climate change poses risks like extreme weather and shifting irradiance, but our strategies mitigate them robustly. We've modeled TCFD scenarios showing 2x portfolio value under net-zero pathways, with 95%+ SLR ESG scores. Actions include black-start BESS for resilience post-Uri, drone inspections reducing downtime <1%, and biodiversity net-gain habitats. Hedges cover 80% debt, curtailment reserves in CAISO, and VPPs for grid stress. Upside from scarcity pricing—$200/MWh ancillaries—and IRA elective pay. Our diversified 52 GW pipeline across regions buffers localized impacts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Michael Chen:
Emily, our projects deliver strong long-term profitability with 12-15% after-tax IRRs, ROIC expanding to 12% by FY26, and 8-10% EBITDA CAGR through FY27. Key to this: LCOE $25/MWh solar, $45/MWh wind via tech deflation; hybrid capacity factors 35-40%; PPA extensions at $38/MWh uplift; and financing WACC 5.8% blending tax equity (7.1% yields, 55-65% ITC) with debt at SOFR+190 bps. Backlog $18.5B at 95% contracted utilization, 20 GW FY25-27 adds, and margin expansion from OpEx deflation (22% since 2022). Risks hedged, with merchant 20% for upside.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time there appear to be no further questions. I will now turn the call back over to Sarah Kline for any closing remarks.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Solara Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
